name: Thorium
occurrence: More abundant in Earth's crust than uranium, found mainly in the mineral monazite alongside rare-earth elements.
majorUses: Proposed alternative nuclear fuel (thorium reactors, potentially safer/more abundant than uranium)
Historically used in gas-mantle lighting (glowing incandescent fabric mesh)
safetyNotes: Radioactive, though its main isotope decays slowly enough (a half-life longer than the age of the universe) that bulk thorium is far less immediately hazardous than many other radioactive elements.
notableCharacteristics: Named after Thor, the Norse god of thunder, and is being actively researched as a potentially safer, more abundant nuclear fuel alternative to uranium.
ncertRelevance: comparison to uranium as nuclear fuel
whyHere: With a slowly-decaying, very long half-life isotope as its dominant natural form, thorium is stable enough to handle in bulk yet still capable of sustaining a nuclear fission cycle when properly configured — exactly the combination researchers hope could make thorium reactors both safer and more sustainable than conventional uranium ones.
didYouKnow: India, which holds one of the world's largest thorium reserves relative to its uranium reserves, has invested heavily in thorium-fuel-cycle nuclear reactor research as a long-term energy strategy.
genZNote: Named after the god of thunder and might genuinely be the future of nuclear power. No pressure on this one either.
